summary:
Found only on the volcanic slopes of Isla Isabela in the Galápagos, the Pink Iguana (*Conolophus marthae*) is one of Earth's rarest reptiles — its blush-toned skin a quiet wonder unknown to science until the 1980s. Fewer than 200 mature individuals survive, confined to a fragment of land no larger than a small town.

Their world is precarious: volcanic eruptions could erase their only home overnight, while invasive rats and feral cats threaten the young. No juvenile recruitment has been observed, meaning this ancient lineage may be quietly fading without replacement. What was once a mystery is now a warning — a species discovered just in time to watch it disappear.
